about: Personal notes (platform.memory, scope personal). 56 live at T (52 active, 4 dormant) and 6 ended rows (3 replaced, 3 deleted). 'source' names the hand-written thread and turn, or 'auto': the kind of background thread the seeder attaches the note turn to, with the manager's own words in 'said'.

notes.subject: Reply drafts
notes.text: Draft replies: offer two appointment times before the price
notes.why: Greg coaches her to offer a time before a price; her drafts led with the price.
notes.how: In any draft to a customer that names a price.

notes.subject: Answer length
notes.text: Keep answers short: the number first, then one line of why
notes.why: She reads answers out to a caller on hold.
notes.how: Every answer; more only when she asks.

notes.subject: Prices source
notes.text: Take prices from the price list page, never from a service page
notes.why: A service page gave a price from before the last labour rise.
notes.how: Whenever a price is quoted or drafted.

notes.subject: Default shop
notes.text: Default my questions to the East Main shop
notes.why: She works at East Main and reads Bonny Oaks only on cover days.
notes.how: When a question names no shop; say that the answer covers East Main only.

notes.subject: Call summaries
notes.text: Summarising my calls: start with what to try next
notes.why: She uses the summary to pick one thing to practise that day.
notes.how: Any summary of her own calls or scorecards.

notes.subject: Money and dates
notes.text: Show money with cents and dates with the weekday
notes.why: She reads figures out to customers, and people come on the wrong day.
notes.how: Every amount and every date, in answers and in drafts.

notes.subject: Prices source
notes.text: Take prices from the price list page, never from a service page
notes.why: He quoted a timing belt from a service page that had the old labour rate.
notes.how: Whenever a price is quoted or drafted.

notes.subject: Two questions
notes.text: When I ask two things in one message, answer both, numbered
notes.why: He acts on the first answer and misses the second.
notes.how: Any message of his that holds more than one question.

source.said: I asked two things and only caught the first one. Can you number the answers when I ask more than one?

notes.subject: Promises
notes.text: Never put 'same day' or a pickup time in a draft unless the order shows the parts in hand
notes.why: He promised a same-day finish before the kit was confirmed, and the car was a day late.
notes.how: Drafts and suggested wording about when a car will be ready.

source.said: After the Daugherty thing: don't let me write same day in a text unless the parts are actually here. Hold me to that.

notes.subject: Shop terms
notes.text: Spell out a shop abbreviation the first time it appears in an answer
notes.why: He is new and looks up terms the others say without thinking.
notes.how: RO, PO, R&R, DVI and the like, once per conversation.

source.said: What's an RO again? Sorry, I'm new. Could you spell these out the first time?

notes.subject: Prices source
notes.text: Take prices from the price list page, never from a service page
notes.why: He found the timing belt page still on the old labour rate and sent in a correction.
notes.how: Whenever a price is quoted or drafted.

notes.subject: Counter screen
notes.text: Short lines and no tables: I read at the counter with a customer in front of me
notes.why: A table does not fit the counter screen and he cannot scroll while talking.
notes.how: Every answer unless he asks for a table.

source.said: cant read a table at the counter. short lines

notes.subject: Out-the-door number
notes.text: Give the out-the-door number: labour, parts, shop supplies and tax in one total
notes.why: He always tells a customer the total they will pay at pickup.
notes.how: Any price or estimate meant for a customer.

source.said: give me out the door. parts labor supplies tax, one number

notes.subject: Call, not text
notes.text: For a customer, give me three talking points for a call, not a message to send
notes.why: He would rather phone than type; a chat sits while he walks a customer out.
notes.how: When he asks what to tell a customer; a message only if he asks for one.

source.said: dont write me a text for him, i'll call. just tell me the three things to say

notes.subject: Promised today
notes.text: Open my day with the cars promised for today, earliest first
notes.why: He lines up the morning's pickups before the phones start.
notes.how: The first question of his day.

source.said: first thing every morning i want the cars promised today, earliest first

notes.subject: Names and times
notes.text: Name the person and give a time in every answer; never 'someone' or 'soon'
notes.why: He hands work out from these answers and needs a name and a deadline to do it.
notes.how: Every answer about people, tasks, shifts or call backs.

source.said: Who is someone? Give me the name and the time, every answer.

notes.subject: The shop
notes.text: 'The shop' means East Main
notes.why: He asked about the shop and got all three.
notes.how: Any question of his that names no shop.

source.said: When I say the shop I mean East Main.

notes.subject: The shop
notes.text: 'The shop' means East Main and Bonny Oaks together, split by shop
notes.why: He plans the two Chattanooga shops as one crew.
notes.how: Any question of his that says 'the shop' or names none; Charlotte Pike only when he names it.

source.said: Change that. The shop is both, East Main and Bonny Oaks, one line each.

notes.subject: Missed calls
notes.text: Count missed calls by desk, never by person: a missed call has no person
notes.why: He asked which advisor misses most and the call log could only answer by desk.
notes.how: Any question that compares people on missed calls.

notes.subject: Roster week
notes.text: My roster week runs Monday to Saturday; show Saturday's desk on its own line
notes.why: Saturday morning at East Main is a short shift with its own pair.
notes.how: Any answer about a week of shifts.

source.said: My week is Monday to Saturday. Saturday desk on its own line: it is a different pair every week.

notes.subject: Late
notes.text: Count a shift as late only past the five minutes of grace in the handbook
notes.why: One minute past is not what he speaks to anyone about.
notes.how: Any count or list of late arrivals.

source.said: Late is past the five minutes in the handbook. Don't show me people who clocked in at 7:31.

notes.subject: Sold work
notes.text: Recommended work sold is counted in jobs, not in dollars
notes.why: A dollar share lets one big job hide ten declined ones.
notes.how: Any figure for recommended work sold, by shop or by advisor.

source.said: That share is by dollars. I count it by jobs: sold out of recommended.

notes.subject: Notes to technicians
notes.text: Messages to technicians: two lines, plain, with the car and the time
notes.why: They read them on a phone between jobs.
notes.how: Any draft addressed to a technician or the foreman.

source.said: Too long for Dustin. Two lines, the car, the time. Nothing else.

notes.subject: Waiting on me
notes.text: What waits on me: shift requests first, then team notes, then cards
notes.why: A shift request has a person standing by for an answer.
notes.how: Any list of what waits for his decision.

source.said: Order it this way from now on: shift requests, team notes, then cards.

notes.subject: Leave next week
notes.text: On Fridays show next week's leave before anything else
notes.why: He builds the next roster on Friday afternoon.
notes.how: His first question on a Friday.

source.said: Fridays I start with who is off next week. Put that first.

notes.subject: Number first
notes.text: Lead with the number, then the table; no story unless I ask
notes.why: She asks for the figure and reads the reasoning only when it surprises her.
notes.how: Every answer to a data question.

notes.subject: Before tax
notes.text: Money before sales tax unless I ask otherwise, and say which
notes.why: She compares shops and months, and tax moves only with the mix of parts.
notes.how: Every revenue, bill or average figure.

source.said: Is that with tax? I want everything before sales tax unless I say otherwise, and say which it is.

notes.subject: Charlotte Pike clock
notes.text: Charlotte Pike's shop system keeps Central time; convert before comparing hours across shops
notes.why: An hour-by-hour comparison put Nashville's morning an hour early.
notes.how: Any figure by hour of day that includes Charlotte Pike.

source.said: Those Nashville hours are off by one. Their system is on Central. Convert before you compare.

notes.subject: Three shops
notes.text: When I ask about one shop, show the other two beside it
notes.why: A number for one shop means little to her without the others.
notes.how: Any figure for a single shop, unless she asks for that shop alone.

source.said: Whenever I ask about one shop, put the other two next to it.

notes.subject: Lost account
notes.text: A lost account is a company account billed on terms with no visit in 90 days
notes.why: The first list mixed in small business customers who come twice a year.
notes.how: Questions about accounts lost, fading or at risk.

source.said: No. Lost means an account on terms that hasn't been in for 90 days. The two-vans-a-year customers don't count.

notes.subject: Estimates
notes.text: Call an estimate an estimate, and say what the data cannot show
notes.why: She takes these figures to her father and to the bank.
notes.how: Any figure built on an assumption or on incomplete records.

source.said: If it's an estimate, call it one, and tell me what the records can't show.

notes.subject: Late evening
notes.text: After nine at night ask no follow-up questions: answer and list the assumptions
notes.why: She works late and wants the answer waiting, not a question.
notes.how: Her messages after 21:00.

source.said: It's ten at night. Don't ask me which period, pick the sensible one and tell me what you assumed.

notes.subject: Tables as files
notes.text: Give weekly tables as a file I can forward
notes.why: She forwarded the first weekly tables to her father.
notes.how: Tables with more than ten rows.

source.said: Can I get that as a file? I want to forward it.

notes.subject: Rounding
notes.text: Round money to the nearest hundred
notes.why: She wanted a quick read of the first monthly figures.
notes.how: Totals in summaries.

source.said: Round these to the hundred, I don't need the dollars.

notes.subject: Sign-off
notes.text: Use the customer's first name in the first line and sign drafts 'Angie'
notes.why: Her customers ask for her by name, and her messages read the way she talks.
notes.how: Every draft to a customer.

source.said: Start with their first name and sign it Angie. That's how I write.

notes.subject: Found work
notes.text: A draft about found work goes: what we saw, the photo, the price, two times
notes.why: She shows the worn part before she names a price.
notes.how: Drafts that recommend work found on inspection.

source.said: Order matters. What we saw, the photo, then the price, then two times to pick from.

notes.subject: Declined last time
notes.text: When I ask about a customer, start with what they declined last visit
notes.why: She brings it up at the counter before anything new.
notes.how: Any customer lookup.

source.said: Lead with what she turned down last time. That's what I'll ask her about first.

notes.subject: My days
notes.text: My numbers are for the days I worked; never average in my days off
notes.why: A weekly average blended her days with the days Josh ran the counter alone.
notes.how: Any figure for her own selling or calls.

source.said: That's the whole week. Take out my days off, those aren't mine.

notes.subject: Recap line
notes.text: End every customer draft with what we do, what it costs and when to pick up
notes.why: She closes every call that way.
notes.how: Every draft that confirms work.

source.said: Close it the way I close a call: what we're doing, what it costs, when it's ready.

notes.subject: Smiley
notes.text: A smiley at the end of a draft is fine
notes.why: Her regulars write to her that way.
notes.how: Drafts to customers she knows.

source.said: A smiley at the end is fine with my regulars.

notes.subject: Document numbers
notes.text: Give every amount with its invoice or statement number
notes.why: She checks each figure against the paper before she uses it.
notes.how: Any amount owed, billed or paid.

source.said: Which invoice is that? Please give the number with every amount.

notes.subject: No rounding
notes.text: Please do not round any amounts at all, show everything to the cent, and make sure the totals add up to the lines above them
notes.why: A rounded total did not match her ledger.
notes.how: Every amount and every total.

source.said: Please don't round. To the cent, and the total has to equal the lines above it.

notes.subject: No rounding
notes.text: To the cent; totals must equal their lines
notes.why: A rounded total did not match her ledger.
notes.how: Every amount and every total.

notes.subject: Days to pay
notes.text: Days to pay run from the statement date to the payment date, not from the visit
notes.why: Counting from the visit added up to a month to every account.
notes.how: Any figure for how fast a company account pays.

source.said: That is counted from the visit. It runs from the statement date to the day the payment is recorded.

notes.subject: Corrected punches
notes.text: List corrected punches with who corrected them and when
notes.why: She pays from the corrected hours and wants to see what changed.
notes.how: Any question about hours worked for pay.

source.said: Show me which punches were corrected, by whom and when. I pay from those.

notes.subject: Part lines
notes.text: One line per part: number, brand, arrival
notes.why: He reads a list of parts the way he writes one.
notes.how: Any list of parts or purchase orders.

source.said: one line a part. number, brand, eta

notes.subject: Part lines
notes.text: One line per part: number, brand, supplier, arrival time
notes.why: He reads a list of parts the way he writes one.
notes.how: Any list of parts or purchase orders.

notes.subject: Facts only
notes.text: No greetings and no adjectives; facts only
notes.why: He reads answers between calls to suppliers.
notes.how: Every answer.

source.said: skip the hello. facts.

notes.subject: On time
notes.text: A delivery is on time when it is received on the promised day, whatever the hour
notes.why: Counting to the hour made the home supplier look late on afternoon drops.
notes.how: Any on-time figure for a supplier.

source.said: wrong. on time = received on the promised day. hour doesn't matter

notes.subject: Late orders first
notes.text: Start with purchase orders past their promised date, oldest first
notes.why: Those are the ones he chases after two o'clock.
notes.how: Any list of open purchase orders.

source.said: late ones first. oldest on top

notes.subject: Nashville time
notes.text: All my times are Nashville time; write CT after them
notes.why: A Chattanooga time on a Charlotte Pike booking is an hour off.
notes.how: Every time in an answer or a draft.

source.said: Is that 8:00 our time? Everything for me in Nashville time please, with CT after it.

notes.subject: Estimate attached
notes.text: Customer drafts name the attached estimate and its total, never a bare price
notes.why: She sends a written estimate with every quote.
notes.how: Any draft that quotes a price.

source.said: I never send just a price. Mention the estimate I'm attaching and its total.

notes.subject: Finished yesterday
notes.text: In my morning summary list yesterday's finished cars so I can ring the owners
notes.why: She makes a follow-up call the day after a repair.
notes.how: Her first question of the day.

source.said: Add yesterday's finished cars to my morning rundown. I call each one.

notes.subject: My desk
notes.text: My desk is 303; calls that rang 302 first are not mine
notes.why: A count of her missed calls included calls that rang the other desk.
notes.how: Any count of calls or misses for her.

source.said: Those aren't mine. I'm 303. If it rang 302 first, it's not my miss.

notes.subject: Plain talk
notes.text: Keep drafts casual: no 'Dear customer', no 'kindly'
notes.why: It does not sound like him and customers notice.
notes.how: Every customer draft.

source.said: Nobody talks like that. Lose the Dear customer.

notes.subject: Promised call backs
notes.text: Open my day with the call backs I promised, oldest first
notes.why: He forgets them once the counter gets busy.
notes.how: His first question of the day.

source.said: Can you start my day with who I said I'd call back? Oldest first. I forget.

notes.subject: Angie in today
notes.text: Tell me first whether Angie is in today
notes.why: On her days off the counter is his alone.
notes.how: His first question of the day.

source.said: First thing, is Angie in today?

notes.subject: Price up top
notes.text: In drafts put the price in the first line
notes.why: He thought customers wanted the number before anything else.
notes.how: Drafts that answer a price question.

source.said: Just put the price up top, that's what they want.

notes.subject: Shop clock
notes.text: Times for Charlotte Pike in Central, always
notes.why: A report gave his opening time an hour late.
notes.how: Every time that concerns his shop.

source.said: We open at 7:30. Central. Fix that.

notes.subject: One line
notes.text: One line. If I want more I'll ask
notes.why: He reads answers on his phone on the shop floor.
notes.how: Every answer.

source.said: Too much. One line.

notes.subject: Plain words
notes.text: Plain words, no tables, three lines at most: I read on the phone
notes.why: He reads on a phone before he reads the paper.
notes.how: Every answer and every scheduled report of his.

source.said: bud i cant read a table on this phone  three lines plain words  Ray

notes.subject: Streets and first names
notes.text: Call the shops by their streets and the people by first name
notes.why: He knows the shops as East Main, Bonny Oaks and Charlotte Pike, and everyone in them by first name.
notes.how: Every answer.

source.said: which one is west  say charlotte pike  and its dale not mr hutchins  Ray
